audit.why: 50.09% over 5989 games — a genuine coinflip. diff EVEN at 5.5/10 fits, and the prose split (Darius owns 1-3, Sett's Grit window at 4-6, even after items) is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[0], win[1], win[2] said Sett and win[5] said Skill, with phases[0..2].side=Sett and phases[5].side=Skill — while whys[0..2] say 'favours Darius', whys[5] says 'First item favours Darius', early says 'Levels 1-3 are yours', and the packet chart reads Darius/Darius/Darius/Skill/Sett/Darius/Skill.
audit.why: Four of seven chart rows contradicted their own why-lines, the breakdown prose and the packet.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 2, 3 and First item flipped to Darius; Levels 4-5, Level 6 (Sett) and 2+ items left as they were.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker (E) only stuns when it catches enemies on opposite sides of Sett; a target on one side is slowed instead. Nothing in the entry says this, and the content layer never names a single Sett ability (packet defect).
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Whether you eat a stun or a slow before his Haymaker is the whole all-in, and it is positional — stay on the same side as his minions and he gets a slow.
audit.corrected: Stated with Facebreaker's 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown, plus Haymaker's true-damage centre versus physical sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Haymaker but gave no numbers and carried boilerplate about dashes Sett does not have.
audit.corrected: Haymaker 18s, Facebreaker 16s and Apprehend 26s at rank 1, with the order to fight in.

edits.before: Your spike early, his at 5: levels 1-3 you out-trade Sett before his Grit shield stacks — Q the edge and stack Hemorrhage. By level 4-5 his W true-damage punch off a full Grit bar can out-burst you if you fed the shield with poke.
edits.after: Your spike early, his at 5: levels 1-3 you out-trade him before Haymaker (W) has Grit — Q the edge and stack Hemorrhage. Facebreaker (E) stuns only if it catches you and his minions on opposite sides, so stay on their side of him.

edits.before: Fill Grit off your poke then W-punch for true damage
edits.after: Store Grit off your damage, then Haymaker's true centre

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours — before Sett's Grit shield fills he's just a slow melee with a slow-charging W, so Q the outer blade, stack Hemorrhage and win the short trades. Keep them short so you never feed his shield with sustained poke.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours — before Grit fills, Haymaker (W) is a slow-charging punch, so Q the outer blade and stack Hemorrhage. Keep trades short so you never charge it, and hug his minion side: Facebreaker slows rather than stuns with you all on one side.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — His shield + burst, fuelled by grit. R after it’s used. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — 18s at rank 1, and its centre is true damage while the sides are physical, so stand off-centre. - Facebreaker: 16s at rank 1; it stuns only across opposite sides, otherwise it slows. - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1 — spend it on his step-up, never on chip, and hold Noxian Guillotine until the Grit shield decays rather than feeding a full bar. Darius Ghost: your run-down enabler once Facebreaker is spent.

edits.before: His shield + burst, fuelled by grit. R after it’s used. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: His shield and burst, fuelled by Grit. It is 18s at rank 1 — commit on its cooldown, never into it.

notes: Chart was wrong in four of seven rows and disagreed with its own whys and the packet. Facebreaker's opposite-sides stun condition is the decisive positional rule in this lane and appeared nowhere. UNVERIFIED, deliberately not written: darius.json flags Noxian Guillotine as a dash and sett.json flags The Show Stopper with 'grounding', which would imply the slam zone denies your R — but Riot's own description of The Show Stopper says only 'dealing damage and slowing all enemies near where they land', no grounding. Per the rule that the description beats a derived flag, I left the claim out; it needs a wiki check before anyone writes it. Packet suspectName 'Fill Grit' is real but not a wrong ability name — Grit is the resource, Pit Grit is the passive; I rewrote the line to name Haymaker instead.
